what_to_do.en: Tap the sentence with the opposite word.

stages.choice_rule: Write four short kid sentences. The stem names one cue word after The word is. Exactly one sentence uses a true antonym of that cue. The other three use the same cue word, a close-meaning word, or an unrelated kid word. Never put two true antonyms in one item. Each choice stays under 60 characters.

roots: Exactly one choice uses a true antonym of the cue word named in the stem.
Wrong choices use the same cue word, a close-meaning word, or an unrelated kid word. Never a second true antonym.
Keep every sentence in kid world: school, home, food, pets, play, family, or weather. No brands.
Choice sentences must be grammatical, tap-friendly, and under 60 characters.
Tier 3 near-misses should be synonyms, milder cousins, or adverb forms of the cue, such as quietly for quiet.
Never use real names in stems or choices. Use only the <NAME> swap token in the stem.

tier_rules.1: Cue stem is The word is plus a common one-syllable adjective. The right sentence uses a clear opposite such as hot and cold or big and little. Wrong sentences repeat the cue, use a near meaning, or use an unrelated kid word.
tier_rules.2: Cue is a grade-two everyday word such as fast, day, or open. The right sentence uses the everyday opposite. One distractor is a close cousin such as quick, noon, or lock.
tier_rules.3: Longer cue with <NAME> or a two-syllable word such as quiet or always. Near-miss distractors use a synonym, a milder cousin, or an adverb form. Only one true opposite.
